rules.heading: Reword a locked claim, never strengthen it
rules.nativeFeature: none in gathered facts (the rule cites a concise built-in output style)
rules.evidence: The gathered facts document output styles only as a plugin component and a cache-safe setting (plugins/components; prompt-caching). Nothing in them describes a concise built-in style that preserves error reports, security warnings, or destructive-action confirmations, so the floor the rule cites cannot be confirmed from this evidence. The locked-span diff check and the decision ledger have no native counterpart.

rules.heading: Treat silence as not approval
rules.nativeFeature: Permission prompt; plan mode; agent-teams inter-agent trust rules; teammate plan auto-approval; dontAsk/-p denial
rules.evidence: The agent-teams docs say a teammate cannot approve a permission prompt or supply consent on the user's behalf, and auto mode treats a relayed approval as untrusted. They also say a teammate's plan request is approved in the lead's session without the lead reviewing it. So the harness already enforces the 'agent message never substitutes' clause and opens a plan-mode gap the rule does not name.
rules.proposedWording: Where the harness gates a write, its permission prompt is the floor, and it already refuses an agent message as consent on a person's behalf; elsewhere, show the diff and wait for an explicit yes before generating a file, since silence is not approval, nor is an unanswered question. Plan mode holds edits until approved, but the hold ends there, does not bind where bypass permissions apply, covers edits rather than every write, and a teammate's plan is approved in the lead's session unread.

rules.heading: Read agreement with a shown suggestion as anchored, not accurate
rules.nativeFeature: skill-creator blind comparator agents; managed Code Review finding reactions
rules.evidence: The skill-creator comparator judges two versions without knowing which is which. The Code Review docs say reactions and replies to findings change nothing on the PR and document no tuning loop, so the rule's claim that the hosted reviewer feeds agreement marks into its own tuning is not supported by the gathered facts. The native blinding primitive is the better floor to cite.
rules.proposedWording: The harness's skill comparator already judges two outputs without knowing which is which; extend that blinding to every human review, since a person's agreement mark on a finding shown to them is an anchored measure, not a quality one.

notes:
I classified all nine rules. No rule is a DUPLICATE and none is a CONFLICT.

Rules I was unsure about:

- "Reword a locked claim, never strengthen it": the rule treats a concise built-in output style as its floor, one that keeps error reports, security warnings, and destructive-action confirmations intact. None of the gathered facts document that style. I classified the rule UNIQUE and left the wording alone because I cannot show it is wrong. Someone should check that citation against the current output-styles doc before the next release; if the style is gone or behaves differently, the sentence needs a rewrite or a cut.

- "Keep a deterministic backbone": the rule says the harness fails a printed run (print mode) on an invalid schema. The facts only confirm schema validation for workflow agent() calls, where the harness validates, retries and then fails. For print mode they list only the plain text, json and stream-json output formats. The rewording widens the anchor to workflow agents, which the facts support. The print-mode schema flag is still unconfirmed and may need its own citation.

- "Read agreement with a shown suggestion as anchored, not accurate": the rule says the hosted reviewer feeds agreement marks into its own tuning. The facts say only that reactions and replies change nothing on the PR; they neither confirm nor deny tuning. I reworded it to cite the blind comparator in skill-creator, which is documented. If the maintainer has a separate source for the tuning claim, keep the original and add that citation.

- "Treat silence as not approval": the harness already enforces that an agent message is never consent (agent-teams trust rules). That part of the rule restates native behavior, but the rule as a whole adds more, so I rated it COMPLEMENT. The rewording also names a gap the facts show: a teammate's plan is approved in the lead's session without review, which supports this rule directly.

- "Quarantine model output until a human moves it": the rewording reflects that auto mode is now the built-in starting mode and auto-approves edits inside the working directory. That makes the write-approval floor even thinner than the rule says, which strengthens the case for the structural gate.

- "Cite or stay silent" is UNIQUE; no evidence gate or citation check exists natively.

- "Report no finding", "Refute with named lenses" and "Gate output on status tags" already cite their native floors accurately and are kept.

The "Don't" section was excluded as instructed. Its Anchor line points back at the rules above, so the proposed rewordings do not affect it.

item: house-rules mechanisms vs native Claude Code harness (plugin at .claude/worktrees/survey-clean/plugins/house)

rules.heading: PreToolUse branch guard (hooks/no-direct-master.sh via hooks.json)
rules.nativeFeature: PreToolUse hook deny, which holds in every permission mode; auto mode's default push allowance; permissions.ask as a text-matched checkpoint
rules.evidence: Auto mode allows pushes to any branch, the default branch included, and the docs say a permissions.ask rule on git push misses git -C or git -c forms and point to a PreToolUse hook for a checkpoint that reads the full command text. The guard is that hook, and it refuses the ways to disarm the git-hook floor that actually enforces branch policy.

rules.heading: SessionStart floor arming (hooks/arm-git-hooks.sh)
rules.nativeFeature: none (SessionStart hook is only the carrier)
rules.evidence: Nothing native sets core.hooksPath or arms a vendored git-hook directory. The closest native protections are sandbox and protected-path write denials on .git and .husky, and neither arms a hook floor.

rules.heading: InstructionsLoaded rule-load logger (hooks/instructions-loaded.mjs)
rules.nativeFeature: InstructionsLoaded hook event; /context memory-file listing
rules.evidence: /context shows which CLAUDE.md and rule files loaded, but only in the live session. The logger uses the native InstructionsLoaded event to keep durable evidence that house doctor can read back later.

rules.heading: Skill: bootstrap
rules.nativeFeature: /init (and /import); disable-model-invocation
rules.evidence: /init generates or improves the codebase-derived CLAUDE.md, and the skill already hands that half to /init while writing only the house manifest and skeleton. It is gated with the native disable-model-invocation field.

rules.heading: Skill: conventions
rules.nativeFeature: none (closest: /context, path-scoped rule auto-load)
rules.evidence: The harness loads path-scoped rules on read, and /context lists what loaded. Nothing native answers which rule covers a topic from an index without loading rule bodies.

rules.heading: Skill: handoff
rules.nativeFeature: session resume (--continue / --resume, full history restored); auto memory; task list
rules.evidence: On one machine, resume already restores the full conversation, and auto memory carries notes across sessions, but auto memory is machine-local and never shared. Handoff adds the checked-in, cross-machine half (issues and recorded decisions). Its opening does not name that native floor.
rules.proposedWording: The harness already resumes a session's full history with --continue or --resume and keeps machine-local auto memory, so the snapshot carries only what those cannot: next steps and decisions another machine or person has to find in the repo or its issues.

rules.heading: Skill: revise-docs
rules.nativeFeature: auto memory; /doctor prompt-audit
rules.evidence: Auto memory captures learnings privately and skips what CLAUDE.md already says, and the skill already names that and routes only the shareable, checked-in half to scoped rule files. /doctor prompt-audit only proposes edits to files that already exist.

rules.heading: Skill: sync
rules.nativeFeature: plugin update / /reload-plugins
rules.evidence: A plugin update refreshes the plugin's own components, but a plugin cannot ship rule context: a root CLAUDE.md is not loaded, and the docs say to use a skill. That leaves the vendored rule files in each repo outside the native update path, and sync is what refreshes them.

rules.heading: Upstream-first sync (sync's refuse-on-local-edit with the upstream PR exit)
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Native rules sharing is symlinks or user-level rules. An upstream edit then reaches every linked project at once, with no pin, no refusal of local edits, and no upstream-first route.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (symlinked rules across projects; user-level rules)

rules.heading: Render and vendor step
rules.nativeFeature: .claude/rules/ with paths: frontmatter; plugin skills with paths: frontmatter; symlinked rules
rules.evidence: The harness loads vendored .claude/rules files natively, and a plugin cannot ship rules. A plugin skill with paths: frontmatter is the documented native route for scoped plugin instructions, and ADR 0001's considered options do not weigh it.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference (instructions must be a skill) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md (paths frontmatter field)
rules.proposedWording: Plugin skills with paths: frontmatter are the harness's own route for shipping scoped instructions in a plugin; they are declined here because every enabled repo takes an update the moment the plugin updates, with no per-repo pin, config, or deviation record.

rules.heading: Lock file (.house/lock.json)
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Nothing native pins or hashes instruction files per repo. Plugin versioning covers the installed plugin, not files vendored into a repo.

rules.heading: Deviations ledger (house.json deviations, mirrored in CLAUDE.md)
rules.nativeFeature: none (closest: claudeMdExcludes, which skips a file but records no reason)
rules.evidence: claudeMdExcludes can drop an instruction file from loading but carries no why, no date, and no ledger.

rules.heading: Ratchets (ratchet and ratchetRaises, ADR 0003)
rules.nativeFeature: startup and /status length warnings for instruction files, per file and combined
rules.evidence: The harness already warns when an instruction file passes the recommended length or the set passes a combined limit. The ratchet adds a per-file ceiling that only tightens and rises only with a recorded reason, and ADR 0003 does not name the native warning.
rules.proposedWording: The harness warns at startup and in /status when an instruction file passes its recommended length or the loaded set passes a combined limit; the ratchet adds what that warning lacks, a per-file ceiling that only tightens and rises only with a recorded reason.

rules.heading: Checker family: drift
rules.nativeFeature: /doctor prompt-audit (references to files or commands that do not exist)
rules.evidence: prompt-audit reports dangling file and command references, but only when someone runs it, and it proposes edits without gating. drift makes the same class a deterministic check that runs every time.
rules.proposedWording: Native floor: /doctor prompt-audit reports references to files or commands that do not exist when someone asks for it; drift makes that class a gate that runs on every check.

rules.heading: Checker family: todo
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Nothing native scans CLAUDE.md for TODO: markers. The /doctor trim check cuts derivable content and does not flag open markers.

rules.heading: Checker family: tamper
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No native mechanism compares an instruction file's body against a pinned source hash. Symlinked rules propagate edits instead of detecting them.

rules.heading: Checker family: behind
rules.nativeFeature: none (plugin update covers the plugin, not the repo pin)
rules.evidence: The native plugin update and 'Not used recently' surfaces track the installed plugin. None of them reports that a repo's vendored pin lags the installed version.

rules.heading: Checker family: shape
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin validate (skill, agent, and command frontmatter)
rules.evidence: claude plugin validate checks a plugin's skill, agent, and command files and can gate CI. It never reads .claude/rules files, so the house rule form (imperative heading, Anchor line, Don't section, em-dash ban) has no native check, and the SKILL.md name check overlaps the validator's scope.
rules.proposedWording: Native floor: claude plugin validate checks a plugin's skill, agent, and command frontmatter; shape adds the house rule-file form, which no native validator reads, and keeps its SKILL.md check to what the validator is not documented to cover.

rules.heading: Checker family: lengths
rules.nativeFeature: MEMORY.md index read limits with write-time reminder and error; instruction-file length warnings
rules.evidence: The header says the auto-memory index is cut at its limit with no notice. The docs say that after Claude writes MEMORY.md, the harness reminds Claude when the file nears a limit and returns an error when it passes one, so the claim contradicts documented behavior. The rule-file length limits themselves complement the native warnings.
rules.proposedWording: The auto-memory index loads every session only up to the harness's line and byte read limits; the harness reminds Claude when a write nears them and errors when one passes them, and this warning covers the edits it never measures, such as a hand edit.

rules.heading: Checker family: coload
rules.nativeFeature: combined-length warning at session start
rules.evidence: The native combined-limit warning counts files loaded at session start. coload sums the path-scoped rules that load together on a read, which that warning never sees.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Large CLAUDE.md startup/status warnings; path-scoped rules)
rules.proposedWording: Native floor: the harness warns when the files loaded at session start pass a combined length; coload adds the per-path sum of path-scoped rules that load together on a read, which that warning does not count.

rules.heading: Checker family: manifest
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No native validator reads house.json. claude plugin validate covers plugin.json and marketplace.json only.

rules.heading: Checker family: minutes
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The native cost surfaces (/usage, modelPricing) cover model tokens, not GitHub Actions minutes.

rules.heading: Checker family: guard
rules.nativeFeature: plugin hooks run only while the plugin is enabled; --safe-mode and --bare skip hooks
rules.evidence: A plugin's hooks fire only in sessions where the plugin is enabled, and safe and bare modes skip them. The guard family warns when a branchPolicy of pr relies on that plugin hook alone and checks the git-hook floor that runs regardless.

rules.heading: Pinned agent roster (agents/*.md)
rules.nativeFeature: plugin agents with model, effort and tools frontmatter; subagent CLAUDE.md and path-scoped rule loading
rules.evidence: The roster uses only supported plugin-agent fields, and each tools list leaves out Agent, so the harness enforces the no-spawn property. The builder's instruction to read CLAUDE.md and matching rules restates native loading, because subagents load project CLAUDE.md and path-scoped rules load on read.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components (agents supported fields) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window (subagent startup context; path-scoped rules)
rules.proposedWording: The harness already loads the repo's CLAUDE.md and each path-scoped rule as you read a matching file, so take them as given; a repo rule wins over this file on conflict.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: session-start injection (hooks/session-start.mjs)
rules.nativeFeature: SessionStart hook additionalContext, re-run on compact
rules.evidence: A plugin cannot ship CLAUDE.md context, so a SessionStart hook with the startup, clear and compact matchers is the native way to keep this text present, including after compaction. claude plugin details reports hooks as having no model context cost, so the plugin's projected cost leaves this always-on text out.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: Roles and Delegation
rules.nativeFeature: subagents for investigation; writer/reviewer pattern
rules.evidence: The best-practices page recommends subagents to keep reads out of the main context and a fresh-context reviewer. The house directives add the split between inline and delegated work and the batching posture.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: Workspace (worktree before first edit)
rules.nativeFeature: --worktree / EnterWorktree, worktree.baseRef, .worktreeinclude, worktree isolation enforcement
rules.evidence: The directive names the harness's worktree tool first but offers a manual git worktree add as an equal route. The docs say manual creation bypasses the base-branch setting and .worktreeinclude.
rules.proposedWording: Enter a worktree before the first edit or branch through the harness's worktree tool; a manual git worktree add skips the harness's base-branch setting and its copy of gitignored files, so use it only when the tool cannot reach the branch you need.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: Model tier (subagent default below the session)
rules.nativeFeature: subagent / teammate / workflow-agent model resolution order; CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL
rules.evidence: The directive says a subagent, teammate, or workflow agent runs below the session by default. Natively, an agent with no assigned model runs on the main conversation's model unless CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is set, and adopters on other machines will not have that env floor.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config (subagent model resolution order) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows (workflow agent model resolution)
rules.proposedWording: The harness runs a subagent, teammate, or workflow agent with no assigned model on the session's model unless CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL says otherwise, so every off-roster call names a model and effort below the session unless the task needs the session's tier.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: Subagents do not spawn subagents
rules.nativeFeature: Agent tool withheld from subagents by default; spawn depth limit
rules.evidence: The harness already leaves the Agent tool out of a subagent's tool set by default, the built-in agents cannot spawn, and the roster's tools lists leave out Agent. The bullet restates enforced behavior to a main session that cannot change it.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: Briefs
rules.nativeFeature: prompt-audit Group 1a (pressure language)
rules.evidence: The ban on 'be thorough' and 'think deeply' matches the pressure-language patterns the bundled prompt-audit flags as over-triggering. The six-section brief and output budget are posture the harness does not supply.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: Parallelism and large workflows
rules.nativeFeature: isolation: worktree; workflowSizeGuideline; Large workflow warning
rules.evidence: Concurrent writers already get the native isolation field. The 'large workflows stay off, name the agent count' line overlaps the native size guideline and warning without citing them.
rules.proposedWording: Workflows run only when the user asks; when they do, name the agent count, and treat the harness's workflow size guideline as advice to stay under rather than a target.

rules.heading: Orchestration defaults: Verification
rules.nativeFeature: verification subagent; /code-review; tools field denying Edit and Write to reviewers
rules.evidence: Best practices recommend a fresh-model refutation and warn that reviewers over-report. The house adds a stop on a verdict with no must-fix instead of a round count, a user checkpoint, and a git-status tamper check around read-only agents.

rules.heading: Eval cases (plugins/house/evals/*/prompt.md and graders)
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin eval (case format, regex and llm graders, no-plugin baseline arm, OS sandbox on Bash grants)
rules.evidence: The cases use the native format. A case's allowed_tools cannot grant Bash or Write, so branch-and-pr runs git only when the command passes --allow-tools, and nothing in the repo records that. The handbook's native-floor lines still say the runner has no docs page and that isolation is not an OS sandbox, while the plugin-evals page now documents the runner and runs Bash grants under the OS sandbox.
rules.proposedWording: Native floor: claude plugin eval runs these cases against its no-plugin baseline arm; a case's allowed_tools cannot grant Bash or Write, so the suite passes them with --allow-tools, and a Bash grant runs under the harness's OS sandbox.

notes:
I read every named file. The checker is split into one entry per family, and the orchestration defaults into one entry per directive group, because their dispositions differ. The handoff skill gets a single entry, even though the task names it twice.

Unsure calls:
1. Render and vendor: classified COMPLEMENT, not a DUPLICATE. A plugin skill with paths: frontmatter is a native scoped-delivery route, but it has no per-repo pin or deviation record, and ADR 0001 never weighed it. That is why this entry is a reword and not a keep.
2. Model tier conflict: the memory note says CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is set on this machine, so the directive happens to hold here. It is false for any other adopter, so I treated it as a conflict.
3. Lengths: classified CONFLICT, but only on the header's "cut with no notice" claim. The family itself complements the native warnings. There is also a possible path mismatch.
